questions.question: A shopkeeper bought 288 oranges for Rs. 115.20. He sold 50 of them at 70 paise each and the remaining at Rs. 46.20. Find his profit or loss.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Cost of 288 oranges = ₹115.20

Selling price of 50 oranges = 50 × ₹0.70 = ₹35.00

Selling price of remaining 238 oranges = ₹46.20

**Formula used:**

Total selling price = Selling price of 50 oranges + Selling price of 238 oranges

Profit or Loss = Total selling price - Cost price

**Calculation:**

Total selling price = ₹35.00 + ₹46.20

⇒ Total selling price = ₹81.20

⇒ Loss = ₹81.20 - ₹115.20

⇒ Loss = ₹34.00

**∴ The shopkeeper made a loss of ₹34.00.**

questions.question: If Δ ABC ~ Δ QRP; area of Δ ABC : area of Δ PQR = 9 : 4; AB = 18 cm and BC = 15 cm, then find the length of PR.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Δ ABC ~ Δ QRP

Area of Δ ABC : Area of Δ PQR = 9 : 4

AB = 18 cm

BC = 15 cm

**Formula Used:**

Ratio of the areas of two similar triangles = (Ratio of the corresponding sides)²

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e056f7cd7d92272fba9098e95f7418cb886f4be71565fcd3158aecfd48fec1f3.png] 

Let the ratio of the corresponding sides of Δ ABC and Δ QRP be k.

Then, k² = (9)/(4)

⇒ k = sqrt{(9)/(4)}

⇒ k = (3)/(2)

Since Δ ABC ~ Δ QRP, the corresponding sides are proportional.

We need to find the length of PR which corresponds to BC.

Let PR = x cm.

Then, (BC)/(PR) = (3)/(2)

⇒ (15)/(x) = (3)/(2)

⇒ 15 × 2 = 3 × x

⇒ 30 = 3x

⇒ x = (30)/(3)

⇒ x = 10 cm

**The length of PR is 10 cm.**

questions.question:
Simplify the following expression. 

[40 - 48 ÷ 4 of 3] ÷ {(6 + 4) - 4 of 4 + 4 + (6 - 4) + (4 × 4) ÷ 4} × 3.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Simplify the following expression:

[40 - 48 ÷ 4 of 3] ÷ {(6 + 4) - 4 of 4 + 4 + (6 - 4) + (4 × 4) ÷ 4} × 3.

**Formula Used:**

Order of operations (BODMAS/BIDMAS):

Brackets, Orders (i.e., powers and square roots, etc.), Division and Multiplication (left-to-right), Addition and Subtraction (left-to-right).

**Calculation:**

First, simplify the expression inside the brackets:

⇒ 40 - 48 ÷ 4 of 3

Order of operations dictates we handle division and multiplication first:

⇒ 40 - 48 ÷ (4 × 3)

⇒ 40 - 48 ÷ 12

⇒ 40 - 4

⇒ 36

Next, simplify the expression inside the curly braces:

⇒ (6 + 4) - 4 of 4 + 4 + (6 - 4) + (4 × 4) ÷ 4

Handle multiplication and division first:

⇒ (6 + 4) - 4 × 4 + 4 + (6 - 4) + (16) ÷ 4

⇒ 10 - 16 + 4 + 2 + 4

Perform addition and subtraction from left to right:

⇒ 10 - 16 + 4 + 2 + 4

⇒ -6 + 4 + 2 + 4

⇒ -2 + 2 + 4

⇒ 0 + 4

⇒ 4

Now, substitute these simplified values back into the main expression:

⇒ 36 ÷ 4 × 3

Perform division and multiplication from left to right:

⇒ 9 × 3

⇒ 27

**The correct answer is option 3.**

questions.question: Find the total amount of debt that will be discharged by 5 equal instalments of ₹200 each, if the debt is due in 5 years at 5% p.a. at simple interest.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the annual instalment be 100%.

Total Debt is the sum of future values of all instalments at simple interest.

Total Debt = 100% + 105% + 110% + 115% + 120% = 550% of the instalment.

Given, 100% = ₹200.

Total Debt = 550% of ₹200 = 5.5 × 200 = ₹1100.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1100.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Time (T) = 5 years

**Calculations:**

⇒ 1st instalment future value = 200 + (200 × 5 × 4) ÷ 100 = ₹240

⇒ 2nd instalment future value = 200 + (200 × 5 × 3) ÷ 100 = ₹230

⇒ 3rd instalment future value = 200 + (200 × 5 × 2) ÷ 100 = ₹220

⇒ 4th instalment future value = 200 + (200 × 5 × 1) ÷ 100 = ₹210

⇒ 5th instalment future value = ₹200 (Paid at maturity, no interest)

⇒ Total Debt = 240 + 230 + 220 + 210 + 200 = ₹1100

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1100.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Instalment Formula

Total Debt = I × T + [I × R × T(T − 1)] ÷ 200, where I is the instalment amount, R is rate %, and T is time in years.

Understanding Debt vs Principal

The "Debt" mentioned in simple interest instalment questions represents the total future amount due at maturity (Principal + total accrued Interest), not the initially borrowed sum.

Compound Interest Instalments

For Compound Interest, the relationship calculates the present value of instalments: Principal = I ÷ (1 + R/100) + I ÷ (1 + R/100)² + ... + I ÷ (1 + R/100)T.

questions.question: A and B, working together, take 15 days to complete a piece of work. If A alone can do this work in 18 days, then how long would B take to complete the same work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A and B together complete the work in 15 days.

A alone completes the work in 18 days.

**Formula Used:**

Work rate of A = 1/Time taken by A

Work rate of B = 1/Time taken by B

Combined work rate of A and B = Work rate of A + Work rate of B

**Calculation:**

Work rate of A = 1/18

Work rate of A and B together = 1/15

Let the time taken by B alone to complete the work be B days.

Work rate of B = 1/B

Combined work rate of A and B:

1/18 + 1/B = 1/15

Solving for B:

⇒ 1/18 + 1/B = 1/15

⇒ 1/B = 1/15 - 1/18

⇒ 1/B = (18 - 15) / (15 × 18)

⇒ 1/B = 3 / 270

⇒ 1/B = 1 / 90

⇒ B = 90

**B alone would take 90 days to complete the same work.**

questions.question: A shopkeeper marks an article at Rs. 150 and sells it at a discount of 25%. He also gives a gift worth Rs. 2.5. If he still makes a 10% profit, then the cost price (in Rs.) of the article is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = ₹150

Discount = 25% of ₹150 = ₹37.50

Gift worth = ₹2.50

Profit = 10%

**Formula used:**

Selling Price (SP) = MP - Discount - Gift worth

Profit = SP - Cost Price (CP)

Profit% = ((SP - CP))/(CP) × 100

SP = CP + Profit

**Calculation:**

⇒ SP = ₹150 - ₹37.50 - ₹2.50

⇒ SP = ₹110

⇒ Profit% = ((SP - CP))/(CP) × 100

⇒ 10% = ((110 - CP))/(CP) × 100

⇒ (1)/(10) = ((110 - CP))/(CP)

⇒ CP = 1100 - 10 CP

⇒ 11CP = 1100

⇒ CP = ₹100

**∴ The cost price of the article is ₹100.**

questions.question: An iron box with external dimensions 60 cm, 40 cm, and 20 cm is made of 1 cm thick sheet. If 1 cm³ of iron weighs 50 gm, the weight of the empty box is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

External dimensions of the iron box: 60 cm, 40 cm, and 20 cm

Thickness of the iron sheet: 1 cm

Weight of 1 cm³ of iron: 50 gm

**Formula Used:**

Volume of the box = External Volume - Internal Volume

Weight = Volume × Density

**Calculation:**

External Volume = 60 cm × 40 cm × 20 cm

External Volume = 48000 cm³

Internal dimensions: (60 - 2) cm, (40 - 2) cm, (20 - 2) cm

Internal Volume = 58 cm × 38 cm × 18 cm

Internal Volume = 39672 cm³

Volume of iron used = External Volume - Internal Volume

Volume of iron used = 48000 cm³ - 39672 cm³

Volume of iron used = 8328 cm³

Weight = Volume × Density

Weight = 8328 cm³ × 50 gm/cm³

Weight = 416400 gm

Weight in kg = 416400 gm / 1000

Weight in kg = 416.40 kg

**The weight of the empty box is 416.40 kg.**

How many students obtained more than the average marks of the class?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The bar graph shows the distribution of marks obtained by students.

**Formula Used:**

1. Average marks = Total marks / Total number of students

2. Number of students who obtained more than the average marks.

**Calculation:**

**Step 1: Calculate total marks and total number of students**

Total students = 1 + 3 + 2 + 8 + 5 + 4 + 1 = 24

Total marks = (1 × 125) + (3 × 130) + (2 × 135) + (8 × 140) + (5 × 145) + (4 × 150) + (1 × 160) = 125 + 390 + 270 + 1120 + 725 + 600 + 160 = 3390

**Step 2: Calculate the average marks**

Average marks ⇒ 3390 / 24 ≈ 141.25

**Step 3: Find the number of students who obtained more than the average marks**

Students who scored above 141.25 are those who scored 145, 150, and 160 marks.

Number of students in these categories: 5 (145 marks) + 4 (150 marks) + 1 (160 marks) = 10

**Therefore, 10 students obtained more than the average marks of the class.**

questions.question: The perimeter of a triangle is 36 units. Its area cannot be more than ______ square units.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Perimeter of the triangle = 36 units

**Formula used:**

Area of a triangle with maximum possible area is of equilateral triangle.

Maximum area of an equilateral triangle = (side²) × (√3)/(4)

For an equilateral triangle, side = (Perimeter)/(3)

**Calculation:**

⇒ Side = 36 / 3 = 12 units

⇒ Area = (12)² × (√3)/(4)

⇒ Area = 144 × (√3)/(4)

⇒ Area = 36√3 square units

**∴ The maximum area is 36√3 square units, so the correct answer is Option 2.**

questions.question: A policeman received information that a thief is at a distance of 1.5 km from him. The thief starts moving by car and the policeman chases him by car. The thief and the policeman are moving at the speeds of 90 km/h and 120 km/h respectively. At what distance (in km) will the police catch the thief?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Distance between policeman and thief = 1.5 km

Speed of the thief = 90 km/h

Speed of the policeman = 120 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Relative speed = Speed of policeman - Speed of thief

Distance = Relative speed × Time

**Calculation:**

Relative speed = 120 km/h - 90 km/h

Relative speed = 30 km/h

Let the time taken to catch the thief be t hours.

Distance covered by the policeman in time t = Distance covered by the thief in time t + Initial distance

120t = 90t + 1.5

⇒ 120t - 90t = 1.5

⇒ 30t = 1.5

⇒ t = 1.5 / 30

⇒ t = 0.05 hours

Distance at which the policeman catches the thief = Speed of policeman × Time

Distance = 120 km/h × 0.05 hours

Distance = 6 km

**The police will catch the thief at a distance of 6 km.**

questions.question: If θ is an acute angle and tan θ + cot θ = 2, then find the value of tan³ θ + cot³ θ + 6tan³ θ cot² θ.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

θ is an acute angle

tan θ + cot θ = 2

**Formula Used:**

tan³ θ + cot³ θ + 6tan³ θ cot² θ

**Calculation:**

Let tan θ = x

Then cot θ = 1/x

Given:

x + 1/x = 2

⇒ x² + 1 = 2x

⇒ x² - 2x + 1 = 0

⇒ (x - 1)² = 0

⇒ x = 1

So, tan θ = 1 and cot θ = 1

Now, calculate:

tan³ θ + cot³ θ + 6tan³ θ cot² θ

⇒ 1³ + 1³ + 6 × 1³ × 1²

⇒ 1 + 1 + 6 × 1 × 1

⇒ 1 + 1 + 6

⇒ 8

**The value of tan³ θ + cot³ θ + 6tan³ θ cot² θ is 8.**
